In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the public has a rather vague idea about psychiatry and psychiatric services, and that the public is not well informed about the role of psychiatrists and psychiatric hospitals.
there is no single approach to psychiatric services organization which would be acceptable to the majority of people.
the respondents have a rather low opinion of psychiatry and psychiatrists.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the public has no definite opinion on the problems of psychiatric service.
a large proportion of the population has no idea about the problems of psychiatry, and the existing knowledge is often based on stereotypes and misconceptions.
in the public opinion the psychiatric service is a service of last resort, which is to be used in the cases of extreme necessity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of the population is in favour of the development of psychiatric services and is ready to support the work of the psychiatrists.

the public opinion of the organization of the psychiatric services is formed on the basis of a set of factors: the attitude towards psychiatry and psychiatrists, the level of information on the problems of psychiatry, the level of knowledge of the problems of psychiatric care organization, the attitude towards the organization of the services and the attitude to the problems of the services organization in general.
